reference_use.conclusion: Snapshot findings (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c). The frozen Contract defines IsoperimetricTheorem, DeformationTheorem, IsLatticeChain, latticeFace and latticeFaceAction as used. SimonGMT supplies covectorEuclideanNorm, massAdmissibleOn, massOn and le_massOn (Mass.lean); VanishesOn, zeroRegion, support = U \ zeroRegion and isOpen_zeroRegion (CurrentLocalEquality.lean); GeometricCurrentOn.ext and the zero current (Currents.lean); and simpleNVector and wedgeCovectors_apply_det (FormsDuality.lean). Mathlib normalises μHE[d] on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) and provides Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, so a ρ-lattice k-face has μHE[k]-measure ρ^k. Mathlib also provides SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate, exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior, PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, AlternatingMap.map_perm, ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq, multilinear map_sum, and Tuple.sort with monotone_sort. There is no Cauchy–Binet theorem in Mathlib (no match), so the covector child uses the elementary constant P^n. Kernel checks in a scratch copy of the frozen project: all five child statements elaborate in the comparator scope and pass validation; NodeSolution `exact Submission.<name>` typechecks; IsoperimetricTheorem follows from DeformationTheorem plus finite_mass, zero_mass_iff and lattice_mass_lower_bound; finite_mass follows from vanish_off_support and covector_eval_bound; and the independent reviewer's ReviewAll.lean proves all five exact statements. All checks use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No lean_name collides with the 26 DAG nodes.

rationale:
Split. Besides the sibling DeformationTheorem, the supplied proof of IsoperimetricTheorem contains three independent, self-contained analytic obligations. (a) Step 1: compactly supported integer-multiplicity currents have finite mass. This rests on two reusable basic facts, kept as separate children: a current annihilates test forms supported off spt T (partition of unity), and evaluating a covector on vectors of norm ≤ 1 is controlled by the Euclidean coefficient norm. (b) Steps 2 and 4: M(T) = 0 ⇔ T = 0. (c) Step 5, Simon's (1): a lattice chain has mass ≥ |β_F|ρ^{m+1} for every face F.

All children are stated generally (in P, n, U, N), help only this parent, and none restates another DAG node. Dependencies are acyclic: finite_mass needs vanish_off_support and covector_eval_bound; the parent then needs finite_mass, zero_mass_iff, lattice_mass_lower_bound and the sibling deformation node.

After the split the parent proof is a short assembly:
- rewrite m+1+(ℓ+1) = m+2+ℓ;
- choose ρ = (2C M(T))^{1/(m+1)};
- |β_F| < 1 with β_F ∈ ℤ gives β_F = 0, so Pc = 0, and M(S) = 0 gives S = 0;
- spt R is closed and lies in a bounded thickening of the compact spt T, hence compact;
- rpow arithmetic gives the exponent (m+1)/(m+2).

Kernel evidence, from a scratch copy of the frozen project (Lean 4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, /tmp/iso_a1_decomp_check):
- All five statements elaborate in the comparator's contract scope (gmt-compare.py contract_scope) and pass lean_contract.validate_lean_statement.
- Comparator-style NodeChallenge/NodeSolution files typecheck with `exact Submission.<name>` against sorry-stubbed declarations.
- IsoperimetricTheorem is kernel-checked from DeformationTheorem plus finite_mass, zero_mass_iff and lattice_mass_lower_bound (Scratch/IsoAsm1.lean, standard axioms; the assembly enlarges C₀ to C₀+1 and also treats M(T) = 0 through the deformation theorem).
- finite_mass is kernel-checked from vanish_off_support and covector_eval_bound (Scratch/IsoC3.lean).
- An independent reviewer agent kernel-checked all five exact child statements and `DeformationTheorem → IsoperimetricTheorem` (Scratch/ReviewAll.lean). This was re-run here: exit 0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The reviewer accepted every child; their lemma-name corrections are folded into the proofs.

The covector bound deliberately uses the constant P^n instead of the Cauchy–Binet constant 1: only finiteness of the mass is needed, and the pinned Mathlib has no Cauchy–Binet theorem. Lean names use the unique prefix isoperimetric_ and collide with none of the 26 DAG nodes.

subproblems.title: Currents annihilate test forms supported off their support
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (C^∞, compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ U): if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T) (zeroRegion(T) = union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T(η) = 0 for every test form η with tsupport η ⊆ W), then T(ω) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) T.support → T ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parenthetical argument in Step 1 of the parent proof ("a test form supported in the open zero region is annihilated: cover its compact support by finitely many open sets on which T vanishes and use a partition of unity"), with Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T), written out for the exact SimonGMT definitions.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Covector evaluation on vectors of norm at most one is bounded by P^n times the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every n-covector α on ℝ^P (continuous alternating n-linear form) and every τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P with ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1 for all j: |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ P^n · covectorEuclideanNorm(α), where covectorEuclideanNorm(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2} and e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), (∀ j, ‖τ j‖ ≤ 1) → |α τ| ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent proof bounds |⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩| using |ξ(x)| = 1 for ξ(x) = ±τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_n with τ orthonormal. Only finiteness of the mass is needed there, so any constant suffices; this lemma supplies the elementary bound with constant P^n (no Cauchy–Binet identity is needed).

Notation. e_a := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1 for a ∈ Fin P; for f : Fin n → Fin P write e_f := (e_{f(1)}, …, e_{f(n)}) and α(e_f) for α applied to this tuple. N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = sqrt(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_I)² else 0)) ≥ 0.

1. Claim: |α(e_f)| ≤ N(α) for every f : Fin n → Fin P.
 (a) If f is not injective, choose i ≠ i' with f(i) = f(i'). The tuple e_f has equal entries in the distinct positions i and i', and α is alternating, so α(e_f) = 0 ≤ N(α) (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq`).
 (b) If f is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort f, a permutation of Fin n such that f ∘ σ is monotone (`Tuple.monotone_sort`). The map I := f ∘ σ is monotone and injective, hence strictly increasing. Since e_I = e_f ∘ σ and α is alternating, α(e_f ∘ σ) = sign(σ) · α(e_f) (`AlternatingMap.map_perm` applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so |α(e_f)| = |α(e_I)|. As I is strictly increasing, α(e_I)² is one of the nonnegative summands whose sum is N(α)², so α(e_I)² ≤ N(α)² and |α(e_I)| = sqrt(α(e_I)²) ≤ N(α).
2. Expansion. For each j, τ_j = Σ_{a ∈ Fin P} τ_j(a) • e_a (expansion in the standard orthonormal basis). By multilinearity of α (expansion of a multilinear map applied to sums and extraction of scalars: `ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_sum` and `map_smul_univ` applied to α.toContinuousMultilinearMap):
 α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_{j ∈ Fin n} τ_j(f(j))) · α(e_f).
3. For every j and a, |τ_j(a)| ≤ ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1 (a coordinate of a Euclidean vector is bounded by its norm, `PiLp.norm_apply_le`). Hence |Π_j τ_j(f(j))| = Π_j |τ_j(f(j))| ≤ 1 for every f (a product of numbers in [0, 1], `Finset.prod_le_one₀`).
4. By the triangle inequality and steps 1 and 3, |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ Σ_f |Π_j τ_j(f(j))| · |α(e_f)| ≤ Σ_f N(α) = card(Fin n → Fin P) · N(α) = P^n · N(α). (For n = 0 the sum has the single empty f, the product is 1 and the bound reads |α()| ≤ N(α).)
proof_key_steps: |α(e_f)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for every f : Fin n → Fin P: zero if f is not injective; otherwise sort f by a permutation σ and use α(e_f ∘ σ) = sign σ · α(e_f).
Expand α(τ) multilinearly in the standard basis: a sum over the P^n maps f of (Π_j τ_j(f j)) α(e_f).
Each coefficient satisfies |Π_j τ_j(f j)| ≤ 1 because |τ_j(a)| ≤ ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1.
Summing gives |α(τ)| ≤ P^n · covectorEuclideanNorm α.

subproblems.title: Compactly supported integer multiplicity currents have finite mass
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every integer multiplicity current T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with compact support spt T has finite mass M(T) < ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n), IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsCompact T.support → T.mass < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 (Finite mass) of the parent proof, written out; it uses the sibling lemmas `Submission.isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support` (key vanish_off_support) and `Submission.isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le` (key covector_eval_bound).

1. Unpack IsIntegerMultiplicity T: there are M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → NVector(ℝ^P, n) with IsRectifiableTriple univ n M θ ξ and T(η) = tauAction n M θ ξ η = ∫_M θ(x) · ξ(x)(η(x)) dμHE[n](x) for every η ∈ TestFormOn univ n. From the triple we use: (i) M is μHE[n]-null-measurable; (ii) θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M; (iii) θ is μHE[n]-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (iv) for μHE[n]-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ, so ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) for every n-covector β.
2. Cut-off. spt T is compact, hence bounded: fix R ≥ 0 with spt T ⊆ closedBall(0, R). Let χ be the smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius R + 1 and outer radius R + 2 (Mathlib `ContDiffBump` on the inner product space ℝ^P): χ is C^∞, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on closedBall(0, R + 1) and χ(x) = 0 when ‖x‖ ≥ R + 2. Put K := closedBall(0, R + 2) (compact and closed, hence measurable) and B := P^n · ∫_{M∩K} θ dμHE[n], a real number by (iii).
3. Splitting. Fix ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n univ, i.e. ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x. Put ω₁(x) := χ(x) • ω(x) and ω₂(x) := (1 − χ(x)) • ω(x). Both are C^∞ and vanish wherever ω does, so they have compact support; hence ω₁, ω₂ ∈ TestFormOn univ n, and ω = ω₁ + ω₂ because χ(x) + (1 − χ(x)) = 1. By linearity, T(ω) = T(ω₁) + T(ω₂).
4. T(ω₂) = 0. For ‖x‖ < R + 1 we have χ(x) = 1, so ω₂(x) = 0: the open ball ball(0, R + 1) is disjoint from support ω₂, hence (being open) also from its closure tsupport ω₂. Since spt T ⊆ closedBall(0, R) ⊆ ball(0, R + 1), tsupport ω₂ is disjoint from spt T, and the sibling lemma vanish_off_support gives T(ω₂) = 0.
5. T(ω₁) ≤ B. By step 1 and linearity of ξ(x), T(ω₁) = ∫_M θ(x) · ξ(x)(χ(x) • ω(x)) dμHE[n] = ∫_M θ(x) χ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμHE[n]. For μHE[n]-a.e. x ∈ M take τ as in (iv); then ‖τ_j‖ = 1, and the sibling lemma covector_eval_bound gives |ξ(x)(ω(x))| = |ω(x)(τ)| ≤ P^n · covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ P^n. Consequently, for a.e. x ∈ M: if x ∈ K then |θ(x) χ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x) · 1 · P^n = P^n · 1_K(x) θ(x) (using θ(x) > 0 and |χ| ≤ 1); if x ∉ K then χ(x) = 0 and the left side is 0 = P^n · 1_K(x) θ(x). The function P^n · 1_K θ is integrable on M, since integrability of 1_K θ on M is equivalent to integrability of θ on M ∩ K (K measurable). Therefore T(ω₁) ≤ |T(ω₁)| ≤ ∫_M P^n 1_K θ dμHE[n] = P^n ∫_{M∩K} θ dμHE[n] = B (the norm of an integral is at most the integral of an integrable a.e. dominating function, `MeasureTheory.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le`; ∫_M 1_K θ = ∫_{M∩K} θ, `setIntegral_indicator`).
6. Conclusion. By steps 3–5, T(ω) = T(ω₁) ≤ B for every mass-admissible ω, so ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B). Since T.mass is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) over mass-admissible ω, T.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B) < ∞.
proof_key_steps: Unpack T = τ(M, θ, ξ): θ > 0 on M, θ integrable on M ∩ K for compact K, and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector of an orthonormal frame for a.e. x ∈ M.
Choose a smooth bump χ equal to 1 on a ball containing spt T and supported in a compact ball K.
For admissible ω, T(ω) = T(χω) + T((1−χ)ω), and T((1−χ)ω) = 0 by the locality lemma since tsupport((1−χ)ω) misses spt T.
Using the covector evaluation bound, |T(χω)| ≤ P^n ∫_{M∩K} θ dμHE[n].
Hence T.mass ≤ ofReal(P^n ∫_{M∩K} θ) < ∞.

subproblems.title: A current has zero mass if and only if it is zero
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P and every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n: M(T) = M_U(T) = 0 if and only if T = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), T.mass = 0 ↔ T = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent proof ("If M(T) = 0 then |T(ω)| ≤ M(T)‖ω‖ = 0 for all ω, so T = 0") and Step 4 (S = 0 because M(S) = 0), made precise for SimonGMT's Euclidean coefficient norm.

Recall T.mass = T.massOn U = sup{ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U}, where ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U means ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ U and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x.

1. (⇐) If T = 0, then T(ω) = 0 and ENNReal.ofReal(0) = 0 for every ω, so the supremum, taken over a subset of {0}, equals 0.
2. (⇒) Assume T.mass = 0 and fix ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Let g(x) := covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) = sqrt(Σ_{I strictly increasing} ω(x)(e_I)²), e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}). Since ω is C^∞, x ↦ ω(x) is continuous into the normed space of continuous alternating maps, and evaluation at a fixed tuple is a continuous linear functional, so each x ↦ ω(x)(e_I) is continuous (`continuous_eval_const`) and g is continuous. Moreover g(x) = 0 whenever ω(x) = 0 (`covectorEuclideanNorm_zero`), so support g ⊆ support ω and g has compact support. A continuous function with compact support is bounded (`Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`): fix B ≥ 0 with g(x) ≤ B for all x, and put c := B + 1 > 0.
3. Homogeneity: for λ ∈ ℝ and an n-covector β, covectorEuclideanNorm(λ • β) = |λ| · covectorEuclideanNorm(β), because every coordinate (λ • β)(e_I) = λ β(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by λ², and sqrt(λ² S) = |λ| sqrt(S).
4. For ε ∈ {1, −1} let η_ε := (ε / c) • ω, an element of the submodule TestFormOn U n. Its support is contained in that of ω, so tsupport η_ε ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ U, and by step 3, covectorEuclideanNorm(η_ε(x)) = g(x)/c ≤ B/(B + 1) ≤ 1. Hence η_ε ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, and `le_massOn` gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(η_ε)) ≤ T.massOn U = T.mass = 0. Therefore T(η_ε) ≤ 0, i.e. (ε / c) · T(ω) ≤ 0 by linearity.
5. ε = 1 gives T(ω) ≤ 0 and ε = −1 gives T(ω) ≥ 0, so T(ω) = 0 = (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U n)(ω). Since ω was arbitrary, T = 0 by extensionality (`GeometricCurrentOn.ext`).
proof_key_steps: (⇐) The mass of the zero current is a supremum of zeros.
(⇒) For a test form ω, x ↦ covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some B ≥ 0.
By homogeneity of the coefficient norm, ±ω/(B+1) is mass-admissible, so ±T(ω)/(B+1) ≤ M(T) = 0.
Hence T(ω) = 0 for every test form and T = 0 by extensionality.

subproblems.title: Mass lower bound for lattice chains (Simon 6.1 (1))
subproblems.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, β : LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) N → ℝ (real coefficients of the faces F = ρ(z + F_α) ∈ 𝓛_{m+1}(ρ) of ℝ^N), and Pc ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^N) with Pc(ω) = Σ'_F β_F [[F]](ω) for every test form ω (IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc). Then for every face index F, |β_F| · ρ^{m+1} ≤ M(Pc) (stated in [0, ∞] as ENNReal.ofReal(|β_F| ρ^{m+1}) ≤ Pc.mass).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ) (β : LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) N → ℝ) (Pc : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) (m + 1)), 0 < ρ → IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc → ∀ F : LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) N, ENNReal.ofReal (|β F| * ρ ^ (m + 1)) ≤ Pc.mass
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 of the parent proof ("Claim: if some β_{F₀} ≠ 0 then M(Pc) ≥ |β_{F₀}|ρ^k … Letting K₀ ↑ F̊₀ gives M(Pc) ≥ |β_{F₀}|H^k(F₀) = |β_{F₀}|ρ^k"), i.e. Simon 6.1 (1) with H^{n−1}(F) = ρ^{n−1}. Here the compact sets K₀ ⊆ F̊₀ are the explicit shrunken faces K_δ, and the coefficients β may be arbitrary reals.

Notation. k := m + 1. For a face index F = (z', α') (z' ∈ ℤ^N, α' : Fin k ↪o Fin N strictly increasing): latticeFace ρ F = {x ∈ ℝ^N : ρ z'_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z'_i + 1) for i ∈ range α', x_i = ρ z'_i for i ∉ range α'}, e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1, and [[F]](ω) := latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = ∫_{latticeFace ρ F} ω(x)(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(k)}) dμHE[k](x). The hypothesis IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc says Pc(ω) = Σ'_F β_F [[F]](ω) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k. Fix F₀ = (z, α) and write A := range α.

0. If β_{F₀} = 0 then ENNReal.ofReal(|β_{F₀}| ρ^k) = 0 ≤ Pc.mass. Assume β_{F₀} ≠ 0 and let s := sign(β_{F₀}) ∈ {1, −1}, so s · β_{F₀} = |β_{F₀}|.
1. The covector dx^α. Let dx^α be the constant k-covector dx^α(v_1, …, v_k) := det[(v_j)_{α(i)}]_{i,j} (in SimonGMT, wedgeCovectors k (fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)), evaluated by `wedgeCovectors_apply_det`). For a strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin N, dx^α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)}) = det[δ_{α(i), I(j)}], which equals 1 if I = α and 0 if I ≠ α. Indeed, if I = α the matrix is the identity (α is injective). If I ≠ α then range I ≠ range α (two strictly increasing maps Fin k → Fin N with the same range coincide, `StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT`), and as both ranges have exactly k elements, some α(i) ∉ range I; row i of the matrix is then zero and the determinant is 0. Consequently: (a) covectorEuclideanNorm(dx^α) = sqrt(1²) = 1, the only nonzero summand being I = α; (b) for every face index (z', α') with α' ≠ α, dx^α(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(k)}) = 0.
2. Boxes. Fix δ with 0 < δ < 1/4. Let K_δ := {x : ρ(z_i + δ) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ) for i ∈ A, x_i = ρ z_i for i ∉ A} and L_δ := {x : ρ(z_i + δ/2) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2) for i ∈ A, |x_i − ρ z_i| ≤ ρ/2 for i ∉ A}. Both are closed and bounded, hence compact; K_δ ⊆ latticeFace ρ F₀ (ρ > 0, δ > 0); and K_δ ⊆ interior L_δ, because the open box {x : ρ(z_i + δ/2) < x_i < ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2) (i ∈ A), |x_i − ρ z_i| < ρ/2 (i ∉ A)} lies in L_δ and contains K_δ (δ/2 < δ and 0 < ρ/2).
3. L_δ ∩ latticeFace ρ (z', α) = ∅ for every z' ≠ z. Let x ∈ latticeFace ρ (z', α) and pick a coordinate i with z'_i ≠ z_i (integers, so |z'_i − z_i| ≥ 1). If i ∉ A, then x_i = ρ z'_i and |x_i − ρ z_i| = ρ |z'_i − z_i| ≥ ρ > ρ/2, so x ∉ L_δ. If i ∈ A, then ρ z'_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z'_i + 1); if z'_i ≥ z_i + 1 then x_i ≥ ρ(z_i + 1) > ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2), and if z'_i ≤ z_i − 1 then x_i ≤ ρ z_i < ρ(z_i + δ/2); in both cases x ∉ L_δ.
4. Cut-off. By the smooth Urysohn lemma on ℝ^N (Mathlib `exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior` on the manifold ℝ^N with model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^N) and smoothness n := ⊤, applied with s := K_δ, which is closed, and t := L_δ, using K_δ ⊆ interior L_δ; `Filter.Eventually.self_of_nhdsSet` extracts φ = 1 on K_δ, and `contMDiff_iff_contDiff` turns the result into a ContDiff function) there is a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^N → [0, 1] with φ = 1 on K_δ and φ(x) = 0 for x ∉ L_δ. Then support φ ⊆ L_δ and tsupport φ ⊆ L_δ (L_δ closed), so φ has compact support.
5. The test form. Let ω(x) := (s · φ(x)) • dx^α. ω is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a constant covector) and vanishes where φ does, so it has compact support and ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k (tsupport ω ⊆ univ trivially). By homogeneity of the coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm(λ • β) = |λ| covectorEuclideanNorm(β), every coordinate being multiplied by λ) and step 1(a), covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) = |s φ(x)| · 1 = φ(x) ≤ 1. Hence ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ and ENNReal.ofReal(Pc(ω)) ≤ Pc.massOn univ = Pc.mass (`le_massOn`).
6. Only F₀ contributes. Let F = (z', α') ≠ F₀. If α' ≠ α, then ω(x)(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(k)}) = s φ(x) · dx^α(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(k)}) = 0 for every x by step 1(b), so [[F]](ω) = 0. If α' = α, then z' ≠ z, latticeFace ρ F is disjoint from L_δ by step 3, so φ and hence ω vanish on latticeFace ρ F, and [[F]](ω) = 0. Thus F ↦ β_F [[F]](ω) vanishes off F₀, and its sum equals its F₀-term (`tsum_eq_single`): Pc(ω) = β_{F₀} [[F₀]](ω). On latticeFace ρ F₀, ω(x)(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(k)}) = s φ(x) · dx^α(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(k)}) = s φ(x) (step 1 with I = α). Therefore Pc(ω) = β_{F₀} · s · ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} φ dμHE[k] = |β_{F₀}| ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} φ dμHE[k].
7. Measures of faces. Let ι : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) → ℝ^N be ι(y)_{α(j)} := ρ z_{α(j)} + y_j for j ∈ Fin k and ι(y)_i := ρ z_i for i ∉ A. Since α is injective, ‖ι(y) − ι(y')‖² = Σ_j (y_j − y'_j)² = ‖y − y'‖², so ι is an isometry. For real a ≤ b, ι maps the cube Q_{a,b} := {y : a ≤ y_j ≤ b for all j} onto {x : ρ z_i + a ≤ x_i ≤ ρ z_i + b for i ∈ A, x_i = ρ z_i for i ∉ A} (given such x, y_j := x_{α(j)} − ρ z_{α(j)} is a preimage in Q_{a,b}). The measure μHE[k] is invariant under isometries (`Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`) and equals Lebesgue measure on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), which gives the coordinate box Q_{a,b} the measure (b − a)^k (`PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin k)`, `Real.volume_Icc_pi`). With (a, b) = (0, ρ) the image is latticeFace ρ F₀, so μHE[k](latticeFace ρ F₀) = ρ^k < ∞; with (a, b) = (ρδ, ρ(1 − δ)) the image is K_δ, so μHE[k](K_δ) = (ρ(1 − 2δ))^k.
8. Lower bound for fixed δ. φ is continuous with values in [0, 1] and latticeFace ρ F₀ has finite μHE[k]-measure, so φ is integrable on latticeFace ρ F₀; φ ≥ 0; K_δ ⊆ latticeFace ρ F₀ is closed, hence measurable, and φ = 1 on K_δ. Hence ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} φ dμHE[k] ≥ ∫_{K_δ} φ dμHE[k] = μHE[k](K_δ) = ρ^k (1 − 2δ)^k (`setIntegral_mono_set`, `setIntegral_congr_fun`). By steps 5 and 6, ENNReal.ofReal(|β_{F₀}| ρ^k (1 − 2δ)^k) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Pc(ω)) ≤ Pc.mass.
9. Letting δ → 0. Step 8 holds for every δ ∈ (0, 1/4). As δ → 0⁺, |β_{F₀}| ρ^k (1 − 2δ)^k → |β_{F₀}| ρ^k; ENNReal.ofReal is continuous and {y ∈ [0, ∞] : y ≤ Pc.mass} is closed, so ENNReal.ofReal(|β_{F₀}| ρ^k) ≤ Pc.mass, which is ENNReal.ofReal(|β F₀| * ρ^(m+1)) ≤ Pc.mass.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to β_{F₀} ≠ 0 and put s := sign β_{F₀}.
The constant covector dx^α = det[(v_j)_{α(i)}] has coefficient norm 1 and vanishes on (e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(k)}) for α' ≠ α.
For 0 < δ < 1/4 choose compact boxes K_δ ⊆ int L_δ, K_δ ⊆ F₀, with L_δ disjoint from every other face of direction α, and a smooth Urysohn function φ (1 on K_δ, 0 off L_δ).
ω := sφ·dx^α is mass-admissible and only F₀ contributes to the lattice sum, so Pc(ω) = |β_{F₀}| ∫_{F₀} φ dμHE[k].
An isometry onto a cube gives μHE[k](F₀) = ρ^k and μHE[k](K_δ) = (ρ(1−2δ))^k.
Hence ofReal(|β_{F₀}| ρ^k (1−2δ)^k) ≤ M(Pc) for all small δ; let δ → 0.
